data.cause: gw.lan's unbound has DNS-rebinding protection (private-address: 10.0.0.0/8) that filters out the 10.20.0.50 answer for .lan names, so whenever a client falls back to the second resolver it gets NOERROR with zero answers (ENOTFOUND); the fallback happens because dns1.lan's aggressive rate limit (20 q/s per /24) intermittently drops legitimate LAN queries, as shown by repeated "ratelimit: 10.20.0.0/24 exceeded ... dropping N queries" log entries.
evidence: dig @10.20.0.3 nas.lan on mon.lan returns 'nas.lan. 10 IN A 10.20.0.50' — dns1.lan answers correctly under normal load
dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan on mon.lan and 'drill nas.lan @127.0.0.1' on gw.lan both return status NOERROR with ANSWER: 0 — gw.lan's resolver yields no address for local names

cat /var/unbound/unbound.conf on gw.lan shows 'private-address: 10.0.0.0/8' and 'private-address: 127.0.0.0/8' (rebinding protection) alongside a forward-zone for lan. to 10.20.0.3; the forwarded answer contains a private address and is therefore stripped, producing empty NOERROR

journalctl -u primary-dns on dns1.lan shows multiple episodes per day: 'ratelimit: 10.20.0.0/24 exceeded 20 q/s, dropping 23/31/19 queries' at 02:14, 09:41 and 13:02, each ending within ~30 s ('back under limit') — matching alerts that occur a few times a day and self-clear in a minute or two
cat /opt/primary-dns/config.yaml on dns1.lan shows ratelimit: 20 applied to the whole LAN, with rewrites answering *.lan as 10.20.0.50
/etc/resolv.conf on mon.lan lists nameserver 10.20.0.3 then 10.20.0.1, so dropped queries cause fallback to the second server
data.recommendation: Fix gw.lan's unbound so it can serve local names: exempt the .lan zone from the private-address filtering (e.g., serve the .lan records as authoritative data/local-zone on gw.lan instead of relying on forwarded answers that contain private addresses). Also raise or scope the ratelimit on dns1.lan (currently 20 q/s per /24) so normal LAN traffic isn't dropped, since those drops are what trigger the fallback path. Both changes are config-only; internet names are unaffected because they don't resolve to private addresses.
data.detail: unbound private-address rebinding filter strips the private IP answers for .lan records, so the fallback resolver returns empty NOERROR for local names
